title.narrative: Digital Access and Rural Empowerment (DARE) Program

description.narrative:
Introduction and Background Rural Ghana faces several systemic issues and challenges that are multifaceted and deeply entrenched. While the youth cohort in Ghana is expected to grow, employment and entrepreneurial opportunities for young people, particularly those living in the country’s economically stagnant rural areas, remain limited, poorly remunerated, and of poor quality. In rural Ghana, young people encounter challenges in accessing and participating in viable economic activities due to limited education, access to finance, infrastructural support, social services, and other productive resources, as well as restrictive cultural and social norms. These challenges significantly impact the lives of the rural youth, affecting their employment opportunities and overall economic advancement. Further expatiating on these barriers, which include: · Limited Educational and Skill Development Opportunities: Rural communities often lack adequate educational infrastructure and resources, leading to lower skilling and literacy rates and educational attainment. This results in the shortage of skills needed to sustain MSMEs in rural areas, thereby limiting the youth's ability to access higher-paying jobs or engage in entrepreneurial activities, as well as impacting the overall productivity of these enterprises, thereby stunting the economic growth of rural communities. · Rise of Adolescent Motherhood: A critical issue in these communities is the high incidence of teenage pregnancy, which not only disrupts young women's education but also places them into a cycle of poverty. The push into early motherhood and the stigma they experience as young single mothers means that the majority of these young women are kept out of dignified work and learning opportunities, making it difficult for them to provide for themselves and their children. · Access to Finance for Entrepreneurship and Innovation: Access to financial resources and services is limited in rural settings. The lack of capital restricts the ability of individuals and households to invest in education, support problem-solving innovations for their communities, start businesses, or even expand their existing businesses. These financial constraints are a significant barrier to personal advancement and economic development. · Infrastructure Deficits: Poor infrastructure, such as inadequate roads, and poor telecommunications connectivity, amongst others, further isolates rural communities, limiting their access to markets, information, and other essential services. Even though some effort has been made to address these by building and equip-ping local Community Information Centers, majority of the CICs are without the needed infrastructure and resources to effectively play the role of information and capacity building centers. · Digital Divide: A significant challenge is the digital divide between rural and urban areas. The digital space is fast evolving with new technologies daily further widening the gap. Limited access to the internet and digital tools in rural communities hinders the youth's ability to participate in the digital economy impacting their access to online information and educational resources, connection to their peers and community re-sources as well as their ability to engage with broader markets for their goods and services. · Cultural and Social Barriers: Cultural norms and social stigmas, particularly around gender roles, further compound the challenges faced by young women, particularly young mothers in rural communities. These barriers deprioritize the needs of these young mothers, often preventing women from pursuing education, participating in the workforce, or engaging in community decision-making processes.
Rural areas account for the highest rates of teenage pregnancy compared to urban areas, according to research conducted by the National Institute of Health. The above-listed challenges are particularly grave for young women, most especially young rural mothers who often raise their children without sufficient family and financial support, lacking basic business skills to be economically active and independent and therefore unable to participate in society as responsible individuals.
The Digital Access and Rural Empowerment (DARE) Program aims to harness digital technologies and the capabilities of Community Information Centers (CICs) to transform rural livelihoods, particularly for young mothers. The program proposes revitalising CICs to serve as digital and technological hubs, facilitating access to information, markets, and essential digital services. These efforts underpin broader development initiatives by serving as platforms for other interventions, including targeted training programs, especially specialized training for young mothers, and also for enhancing market access for rural youths.
The DARE program focuses on three key intervention areas: · Enhanced Connectivity and Market Access · Fostering Rural Youth-Led Business Innovation · Rural Young Mother Economic Empowerment These interventions are interlinked, each designed to address specific challenges while collectively working towards the overarching goal of the improved well-being of rural youth through digital inclusion. This systemic approach ensures that the benefits realized in one area of intervention amplify the impact in others, creating a holistic model of development that caters to the unique needs of rural young women, especially young mothers, and the broader ecosystem of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) they operate within.
UNESCO will implement this project as part of a consortium with the Ghana-India Kofi Annan Center of Excellence in ICT (GI-KACE) and the University of Ghana Business School (UGBS). UNESCO implement intervention - Rural Young Mother Economic Empowerment.
